newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air Canada seen boosting Quebec tourism.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada seen boosting Quebec tourism.

text.p: Tourism prospects for Quebec on the German market will be boosted by plans for a daily Air Canada flight to Montreal, Quebec tourism officials said in a statement issued here on Thursday.

Francois Goulet, marketing director of Tourisme Quebec, said the airline's non-stop code-share service with Deutsche Lufthansa due to start June 15, 1997, could help visitor numbers top 100,000 for the first time next year.
"Air Canada will operate five non-stop flights between Montreal and Frankfurt and two direct flights with a stop in Halifax," he added in the statement.
Quebec has re-opened a tourist office in Germany to try to raise the number of tourists visiting the French-speaking Canadian province to more than 100,000 in 1997, he added.
Some 82,000 Germans are expected to visit Quebec this year, spending about C50 million, compared to 78,000 visitors last year and 60,400 in 1990, Goulet said.
